title: Smartphone-Based Phenotyping of Suicidality and Interpersonal Risk Factors – An Ecological Momentary Assessment Study
summary: Suicide remains a serious issue – suicide rates have hardly decreased in recent years, and in some cases, have even risen. To better understand suicidality and prevent it more effectively, more precise and real-time data collection is needed. One particularly vulnerable group is people with chronic depression. The SMART-SI study is therefore investigating how suicidal thoughts and behaviors develop in the everyday lives of people with chronic depression – especially in relation to interpersonal factors such as loneliness or social isolation. Smartphones are used in this process: participants regularly answer short questions on their phones (Ecological Momentary Assessment, EMA), which creates a detailed picture of their well-being. In addition, smartphone sensor data – such as movement and communication patterns – are collected (Mobile Sensing) to gain more objective insights into potential risk factors. The results will be compared with those from a healthy control group. In the long term, the research aims to improve the detection of suicidality and to develop digital, real-time support tools (Ecological Momentary Interventions, EMI) that can be integrated into existing therapeutic approaches.
conditions: Recurrent depressive disorder, current episode moderate
Recurrent depressive disorder, current episode severe without psychotic symptoms

interventions.name: SMART-SI investigates the dynamic relationship between interpersonal risk factors and suicidality in individuals with chronic depression using EMA and mobile sensing, compared to control participants without mental disorders.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Included are individuals who
- meet the diagnostic criteria for chronic depression according to DSM-5,
- give their informed consent,
- have sufficient knowledge of the German language,
- are being treated at the Department of Psychiatry and Psychotherapy of the LMU Munich.
Exclusion criteria:
Excluded are individuals who
- do not meet the diagnostic criteria for chronic depression according to DSM-5,
- are unable to provide informed consent,
- do not have sufficient knowledge of the German language to answer the questions,
- report severe somatic complaints,
- are unable to receive treatment at the Department of Psychiatry and Psychotherapy of the LMU Munich,
- or exhibit cognitive impairments that make participation in the study impossible.
